stories.title: McKinsey warns AI slows human decisions
stories.summary: A new McKinsey report highlights that while AI accelerates business analysis, human decision making is struggling to keep pace. The firm notes this imbalance could increase strategic risks and hinder the development of future business leaders. AI is creating a speed gap that humans are currently filling.

stories.title: BCG says two thirds of people are now proficient in AI
stories.summary: Sixty four percent of people are now proficient in AI, up 10 percentage points from 2024, according to Boston Consulting Group. The firm says exposure to AI improves perception by sevenfold. Only 7 percent of those surveyed report having no knowledge of the technology at all.

stories.title: NTPC is sole bidder for coal gasification scheme
stories.summary: NTPC was the only company to bid in the second round of India's INR375bn coal gasification incentive scheme. The state-owned power producer submitted two applications for urea, methanol and dimethyl ether production. The first round of the scheme attracted seven applicants. Interest has cooled since September.

stories.title: MECON and EY partner to boost Jharkhand investment
stories.summary: MECON Limited and Ernst and Young have signed a memorandum of understanding to promote industrial investment in Jharkhand. The partnership aims to identify new opportunities, simplify processes and support infrastructure development by combining the technical knowledge and business expertise of both organisations. The state is seeking new investors.

stories.title: Corporate India faces auditor transition
stories.summary: Incoming auditors may face a dual transition as they familiarise themselves with new businesses while assessing financial statements under a new reporting framework. Deloitte audit leader Samir Shah noted that outgoing and incoming firms will likely overlap during the 2027-28 financial year. The handover is underway.

stories.title: Net direct tax collections rise 11.8 percent
stories.summary: Net direct tax collections reached INR14.42 trillion as of November 10, accounting for 53.5 percent of the FY27 budget estimate. While gross receipts grew 14 percent, a 25.9 percent jump in refunds moderated the net growth. Corporate taxes led the increase in the provisional data.

stories.title: NITI Aayog seeks gold mining evaluation matrix
stories.summary: NITI Aayog CEO Anurag Jain has called for a robust evaluation matrix to award mining projects, aiming to improve technical competence and attract investment. Discussions focused on India's untapped gold potential and the country's growing dependence on imports. The policy report was prepared by Pahle India Foundation.

stories.title: NITI Aayog highlights gold mining hurdles
stories.summary: NITI Aayog is deliberating on a report regarding India's gold mining policy, citing geological data gaps and prolonged project timelines as key challenges. The Aayog aims to strengthen domestic exploration capabilities to reduce reliance on imports. The current auction design remains a point of focus for reform.

stories.title: NITI Aayog study on Viksit Bharat and Net Zero
stories.summary: A study by NITI Aayog suggests that achieving the Viksit Bharat goal by 2047 is compatible with reaching Net Zero emissions by 2070. The report outlines the economic and environmental pathways for the country to pursue both targets simultaneously. The findings were released by the government agency.

stories.title: Homestay sector grows in India
stories.summary: India's tourism industry is seeing a shift as travellers increasingly choose homestays over conventional hotels. The trend is expanding from coastal communities to rural locations, offering property owners additional income. Travellers are seeking local food and traditions. Hospitality is becoming a more personal experience for many visitors.

stories.title: VoiceAI rollout faces linguistic and technical hurdles
stories.summary: India's conversational AI market is estimated at $500-550 million, with a potential $4 billion opportunity. However, linguistic diversity, dialect variations and legacy technology continue to complicate mainstream adoption. Enterprises are struggling to implement accurate, low-latency systems across the country. The shift remains a work in progress.

stories.title: Productivity seen as key to manufacturing growth
stories.summary: India's ambition to become a leading manufacturing hub requires a productivity revolution to influence innovation and market leadership. Significant investments are being directed toward this objective, which is now framed as a national imperative. Productivity is described as the primary differentiator for future economic resilience and value creation.

stories.title: Congress questions government data on pollution deaths
stories.summary: The Congress party has accused the government of denying the impact of air pollution on mortality. Citing a FICCI-EY report that attributes 2 million deaths to pollution in 2023, the party challenged the government's previous rejections of studies that were not India-specific. The debate over health data continues.

stories.title: Transport minister raises Qantas cyber security concerns
stories.summary: Transport Minister Catherine King has expressed concern that Qantas may lose control over data by outsourcing 850 head-office jobs to Accenture. The minister referenced recent third-party breaches, such as the attack on Amadeus, as a reason for caution. The airline plans to move services to the consultancy.

stories.title: Qantas to cut 850 jobs in Accenture deal
stories.summary: Qantas will cut 850 corporate jobs as it shifts finance, procurement, human resources and marketing services to Accenture. The changes will begin by mid-2027. Work will be delivered by teams in India and Australia. The airline says the move is intended to modernise its back-office systems.

stories.title: Qantas shifts corporate work to India
stories.summary: Qantas is cutting 850 Australian jobs in finance, procurement, HR and marketing as part of a multi-year deal with Accenture.
